newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-ALLENBY READY FOR MAJOR FITNESS TEST.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ALLENBY READY FOR MAJOR FITNESS TEST.

text.p: Accident-prone Australian Robert Allenby says he is back to the form which almost took him to the top of last year's European rankings after an intensive fitness programme.

At the end of last season, Allenby, crippled from injuries, tapped a shot just a few yards off the first tee at Valderrama to earn his Volvo Masters finishing bonus and ensure he ended in third place in the rankings.
Prior to that he had suffered two accidents in quick succession.

First he fell over a fence and cracked an ankle bone in August in Scotland after the Loch Lomond Invitational, then a couple of weeks later, while recuperating in Spain, broke his sternum in a car accident.
Hence the tap off the tee in the final event of the season which was all he needed to ensure the bonus points. He then retired from the event and spent the next weeks recovering from his injuries.
By his own admission he tried to come back too quickly, returning after only two months layoff when he had been advised to take three months away.
That set him back and the last two months have been a tough rehabilitation with three missed cuts, including at the U.S. Masters.
Right up to last weekend's British PGA, Allenby was seen to be favouring a shoulder, a stiffness stemming from his sternum injury.

However, the young Australian, in Germany for the European Tournament Players' Championship, says he is fit again and aiming to peak around the time of the third major of the year, the British Open in July -- although he forecasts he might be close to good form in two weeks time for the U.S. Open.
"I just tried to come back too quickly," said Allenby, "but I couldn't wait to get back on the course. I've had to hold myself back and now I'm feeling the effects of a strict programme in the gym.
"I've been working for at least an hour each day, often much longer, stretching exercises mainly. Last week's shoulder problem came out of the blue, just stiffness."

Allenby added: "It would be nice to hit form by the U.S. Open but I reckon I might peak for the French Open next month when I defend and then the British Open. I'm fully expecting to play well here in Hamburg, though."
